issue.title: test_app_import_budget: TUI app import loads 3292 modules against a 3290 budget (deterministic, unattributed)
issue.description:
tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py::test_tui_app_import_stays_under_startup_budget
fails deterministically with `assert 3292 < 3290` (_MAX_MODULE_COUNT = 3290, line 13):
importing sase.ace.tui.app loads 3292 modules in a fresh interpreter, two over budget.

This is the module-count assertion, not the wall-clock flake tracked and closed as
sase-136 (which switched the elapsed check to process CPU time).

Found 2026-09-20 in workspace sase_31 while verifying an unrelated change. The count is
exactly 3292 in every run and at each of the five most recent commits (244442ee8,
9cfb06a54, 9231c9352, 65c8169f9, e65cc22ee, each run in a detached worktree), so no recent
commit moved it. A constant, environment-shaped number suggests the total depends on the
interpreter (this venv is Python 3.14) and the installed plugin set (sase-github and
sase-research-artifacts are installed by `just install`) rather than on master. Unverified
whether CI or other workspaces see the same count; confirm that first, then either raise
the budget with a recorded reason or cut two module imports from the TUI startup path.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: The module count is exactly 3292 on every run and at all five most recent commits checked in detached worktrees; it is a counted integer, not a wall-clock measurement, so it cannot vary with load. A rerun on the same tree never passed.

evidence.note: Independently reproduced 2026-09-20 in workspace sase_33 at clean master 86ff62c08 (also with my 2-file diff stashed): tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py::test_tui_app_import_stays_under_startup_budget fails deterministically in isolation with 'assert 3292 < 3290'. Surfaced when the diff-scoped lane escalated to the full suite during sase-iu.

Independently reproduced on a stashed-clean tree at master 86ff62c08: tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py::test_tui_app_import_stays_under_startup_budget fails with the identical `assert 3292 < 3290`. Useful attribution data: a change that added 3 non-TUI modules (service/effective_env.py, lease retryability imports) left the count at exactly 3292 before and after, so the overage pre-dates it and those modules are outside the TUI import chain.

payload.entry: ROOT CAUSE AND FIX (found by the sase-11y.7 gate repair, 2026-09-20, workspace sase_32): the overrun is attributable, not unattributed or environment-shaped. Importing sase.ace.tui.app in a clean interpreter loads 3285 modules at eaa1cbf4d (before the Services-tab phase; passes the 3290 cap), 3292 at 244442ee8 and at 6087c0a8e. Six of the added modules are sase.service.{status,boot,config,paths,state,control}, pulled by two eager import edges that the sase-11y.7 phase added: src/sase/ace/tui/actions/axe_display/_data.py (c2befdbb3, module-level imports of sase.service.control/paths/status) and src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/bgcmd_list.py (92dd554c4, sase.service.status imported for a runtime isinstance check). The sase-11y.7 gate-repair change defers both (TYPE_CHECKING plus function-local imports inside the service-host-enabled branch; duck-typed enablement check) and does NOT raise the cap: the count is now 3286 and only sase.service and sase.service.restart are loaded. tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py now also asserts sase.service.status and sase.service.control are absent after the import, so a future eager edge fails with a named module. The change sits in that worktree pending its host-owned commit; once it lands this bead can be closed on evidence. One further module of the 3285 to 3292 growth is not attributed here; 3286 is 4 under the cap.
